laws.subject: Murder
laws.description: Whoever commits murder intentionally causes the death of another human being or inflicts bodily injury known to be sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death.
laws.key_changes: Section number shifted from 302 to 103(1). Section 103(2) introduces a historic new penal clause for mob lynching and hate crime murders by five or more persons.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 302): Death or Imprisonment for Life, and Fine.
New Law (BNS 103(1)): Death or Imprisonment for Life, and Fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Non-Compoundable | Triable exclusively by Court of Session.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Immediate FIR under Section 173 BNSS is mandatory. Mandatory crime scene videography and forensic investigation under Section 176(3) BNSS applies.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. Murder requires the intentional taking of life without legal justification.

laws.old_law: Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860 - Section 302 (Read with Sec 34 / 149)
laws.subject: Mob Lynching and Hate Crime Murders
laws.description: Murder committed by a group of five or more persons acting in concert on grounds of race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language, or personal belief.
laws.key_changes: New dedicated statutory provision. For the first time in Indian penal history, mob lynching is explicitly defined and penalized as a distinct heinous crime.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law: Charged under IPC 302 read with Section 149 (unlawful assembly).
New Law (BNS 103(2)): Death or Imprisonment for Life, and mandatory Fine for each member.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Non-Compoundable | Triable by Court of Session.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Victims or witnesses can seek witness protection under Section 398 BNSS and the Witness Protection Scheme. Zero FIR can be filed at any station.
laws.full_statutory_text: When a group of five or more persons acting in concert commits murder on ground of race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief or any other ground, each member shall be punished with death or life imprisonment.

laws.subject: Culpable Homicide Not Amounting to Murder
laws.description: Causing death with the intention of causing death or bodily injury likely to cause death, but under mitigating circumstances such as grave and sudden provocation or sudden fight.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned from IPC Section 304 to BNS Section 105. Clarifies categories based on intent versus knowledge.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 304 Part I/II): Life imprisonment or up to 10 years and fine.
New Law (BNS 105): Imprisonment for life or imprisonment up to 10 years with fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Non-Compoundable | Court of Session.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Requires proving the absence of premeditation or presence of grave and sudden provocation to distinguish from Section 103 murder.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever causes death by doing an act with intention of causing death or bodily injury likely to cause death, without premeditation, is guilty of culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

laws.subject: Death by Rash or Negligent Act & Hit-and-Run
laws.description: Causing the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, including vehicular collisions and medical negligence.
laws.key_changes: Section 106(1) handles ordinary negligence (imprisonment up to 5 years). Section 106(2) creates a severe hit-and-run penalty (up to 10 years) for motorists who flee without reporting to police.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 304A): Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
New Law (BNS 106(1)): Imprisonment up to 5 years and fine. (BNS 106(2) Hit-and-run): Up to 10 years and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Section 106(1) is Bailable; Section 106(2) is Non-Bailable | Cognizable | Triable by Magistrate of First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Drivers involved in accidents must immediately inform police or magistrate to avoid the stringent 10-year hit-and-run penalty under Section 106(2). Victims are entitled to MACT compensation.
laws.full_statutory_text: Section 106(1): Whoever causes death by rash or negligent act shall be punished with imprisonment up to five years and fine. Section 106(2): Whoever escapes without reporting shall face up to ten years.

laws.subject: Dowry Death
laws.description: Death of a woman caused by burns, bodily injury, or unnatural circumstances within seven years of marriage, where she was subjected to cruelty in connection with demands for dowry.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned from IPC Section 304B to BNS Section 80. Statutory presumption of abetment continues under modern BSA Section 118.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 304B): Imprisonment not less than 7 years, extending to life.
New Law (BNS 80): Imprisonment not less than 7 years, extending to life.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Non-Compoundable | Court of Session.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Preserve all records of harassment, dowry demands, messages, and bank transfers. Inquest by Executive Magistrate is mandatory under Section 196 BNSS.
laws.full_statutory_text: Where the death of a woman is caused within seven years of marriage under abnormal circumstances and cruelty for dowry is shown, husband and relatives are deemed to have caused dowry death.

laws.subject: Abetment of Suicide
laws.description: Instigating, conspiring, or intentionally aiding any person to commit suicide.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned from IPC Section 306 to BNS Section 108. Direct active instigation or continuous harassment driving the deceased to suicide must be substantiated.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 306): Imprisonment up to 10 years and fine.
New Law (BNS 108): Imprisonment up to 10 years and liable to fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Non-Compoundable | Court of Session.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Suicide notes, digital communications, WhatsApp chats, and eyewitness testimony must be preserved under Section 63 BSA certificate for trial.
laws.full_statutory_text: If any person commits suicide, whoever abets the commission of such suicide shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and fine.

laws.subject: Attempt to Commit Suicide to Compel Public Authority
laws.description: Attempting suicide with the specific intent to compel or restrain any public servant from discharging official duty.
laws.key_changes: General attempt to commit suicide is no longer a crime under BNS (decriminalized in line with Mental Healthcare Act 2017). Only acts of suicide intended to coerce public servants remain punishable.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 309): Simple imprisonment up to 1 year or fine for all suicide attempts.
New Law (BNS 226): Simple imprisonment up to 1 year, or with fine, or with community service.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Bailable | Any Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Citizens in psychological distress cannot be arrested or prosecuted under Indian penal law. They are entitled to medical and psychiatric care.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever attempts to commit suicide with intent to compel or restrain any public servant from exercising official duties shall be punished with imprisonment up to one year, fine, or community service.

laws.old_law: State Anti-Gangster Acts / Special Laws (No dedicated IPC provision)
laws.subject: Organized Crime Syndicates
laws.description: Continuing unlawful activity including kidnapping, robbery, extortion, contract killing, economic offenses, and cybercrimes committed by a syndicate using violence or coercion.
laws.key_changes: Major structural innovation. For the first time, comprehensive provisions against organized crime and mafia syndicates are codified in the general penal law of India.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law: Charged under state statutes (MCOCA, UP Gangsters Act).
New Law (BNS 111): If death results: Death or life imprisonment and min. Rs. 10 Lakh fine. Other cases: Min. 5 years extending to life.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Special Court or Court of Session.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Stringent bail conditions apply. Attachment of proceeds of crime and properties obtained through syndicate operations is authorized under BNSS.
laws.full_statutory_text: Any continuing unlawful activity including extortion, land grabbing, contract killing, and financial scams by members of an organized crime syndicate is punishable under Section 111 BNS.

laws.subject: Petty Organized Crime
laws.description: Theft, snatching, cheating, unauthorized sale of tickets, and betting committed by members of a gang or group causing widespread insecurity.
laws.key_changes: Novel statutory category targeting habitual street gangs, pickpocketing rings, and organized snatching networks that previously evaded stringent custody.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law: Individual misdemeanor charges under IPC 379/420.
New Law (BNS 112): Imprisonment for not less than 1 year which may extend to 7 years, and liable to fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Magistrate of First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Citizens can report repeated localized gang theft or public cheating networks under this section to enable police to invoke syndicate investigation powers.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever commits petty organized crime including organized snatching, pickpocketing, or unauthorized ticketing as part of a gang shall be punished with imprisonment between 1 and 7 years.

laws.subject: Terrorist Acts under General Penal Code
laws.description: Acts committed with intent to threaten the unity, integrity, sovereignty, or security of India, or to strike terror in the people through bombs, lethal weapons, or hazardous substances.
laws.key_changes: Terrorism is codified directly into the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, alongside parallel provisions in the Special Act (UAPA, 1967).
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law: UAPA Sections 15 & 16.
New Law (BNS 113): If death results: Death or life imprisonment and fine. In other cases: Imprisonment from 5 years to life, and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Special Court / Court of Session.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Investigation must be conducted by officers not below rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) or Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP).
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever does any act with intent to threaten the sovereignty or integrity of India, or strikes terror in the people using explosive substances or cyber weapons, commits a terrorist act.

laws.subject: Voluntarily Causing Grievous Hurt
laws.description: Causing permanent privation of sight, hearing, loss of limb, bone fracture, or bodily pain lasting 20 days or endangering life.
laws.key_changes: IPC 325 and 326 consolidated into BNS Section 117. Clear categorization for hurt caused by dangerous weapons.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 325/326): Up to 7 years or life imprisonment for dangerous weapons.
New Law (BNS 117): Up to 7 years and fine; extending to 10 years or life if dangerous weapons used.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable (if weapons used) | Magistrate of First Class / Sessions.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Obtain an immediate Medico-Legal Certificate (MLC) from a government hospital detailing fractures or injuries to establish grievous hurt.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever voluntarily causes grievous hurt shall be punished with imprisonment up to seven years and fine; if by dangerous weapons, imprisonment may extend to life.

laws.subject: Acid Attack and Permanent Disfigurement
laws.description: Throwing acid or administering acid to cause permanent or partial damage, deformity, or disfigurement to any part of the body.
laws.key_changes: Consolidated into BNS Section 124. Retains mandatory minimum sentencing and fine payable directly to the victim for medical rehabilitation.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 326A): Min. 10 years extending to life, and fine.
New Law (BNS 124(1)): Min. 10 years extending to life imprisonment, and fine to cover victim treatment.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Non-Compoundable | Court of Session.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Under Supreme Court rulings and Section 396 BNSS, all private and public hospitals must provide immediate free first-aid and medical treatment to acid attack victims.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever causes permanent disfigurement by throwing acid shall be punished with imprisonment not less than ten years extending to life, and fine just and reasonable to meet medical expenses.

laws.subject: Kidnapping and Abduction
laws.description: Taking or enticing any minor (under 18 years) or person of unsound mind out of the keeping of the lawful guardian without consent.
laws.key_changes: Age threshold standardized to 18 years across genders. Stringent penalties for kidnapping for ransom or human trafficking.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 363): Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
New Law (BNS 137): Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine; if for ransom or trafficking, life imprisonment or death.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Magistrate of First Class / Sessions.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Report immediately to 112 or local station. Missing child complaints must be registered immediately as FIR under Section 173 BNSS without preliminary inquiry.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever takes or entices any child under eighteen years out of the custody of lawful guardians commits kidnapping and shall be punished with imprisonment up to seven years and fine.

laws.subject: Act Endangering Sovereignty, Unity and Integrity of India
laws.description: Purposely exciting secession, armed rebellion, subversive activities, or encouraging feelings of separatist activities endangering the sovereignty or unity of India.
laws.key_changes: Colonial offense of 'Sedition' (Rajdroha) is abolished. Replaced by Deshdroha (acts endangering sovereignty). Disaffection toward government is no longer an offense; armed subversive acts are penalized.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 124A): Up to 3 years or life imprisonment.
New Law (BNS 152): Imprisonment for life or imprisonment up to 7 years, and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Court of Session.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Legitimate criticism, democratic dissent, or peaceful opposition to government policies is protected under the Explanation to Section 152.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever knowingly excites or attempts to excite secession or armed rebellion or separatist activities endangering sovereignty of India shall be punished with life imprisonment or up to seven years.

laws.subject: Unlawful Assembly and Rioting
laws.description: Assembly of five or more persons with common object to overawe public authorities, resist execution of law, commit criminal trespass, or use force or violence.
laws.key_changes: Modernized structure under Sections 189-191 BNS. Community service options available for minor public order disturbances.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 147): Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
New Law (BNS 191): Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both; if armed with deadly weapons, up to 5 years.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Bailable | Any Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Audio-video evidence recorded by citizens or CCTV footage can be submitted to establish lack of common object or non-participation.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whenever force or violence is used by an unlawful assembly in prosecution of a common object, every member is guilty of rioting and liable to imprisonment up to two years.

laws.subject: Affray and Public Fighting
laws.description: When two or more persons, by fighting in a public place, disturb the public peace.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned to Section 194 BNS with expanded provisions for community service as an alternative to incarceration.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 160): Imprisonment up to 1 month or fine up to Rs. 100.
New Law (BNS 194): Imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to Rs. 5,000, or community service.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Bailable | Any Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: First-time minor street altercations can be settled through community service under the new reformative justice framework.
laws.full_statutory_text: When two or more persons fight in a public place and disturb public peace, they commit affray and shall be punished with imprisonment up to one month, fine, or community service.

laws.subject: Harbouring Offender
laws.description: Concealing, providing shelter, food, money, or assistance to a person known or believed to have committed an offense, with intent to screen them from legal punishment.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned from IPC Section 212 to BNS Section 249. Preserves statutory exemption for husband or wife harbouring their spouse.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law: Up to 5 years (for capital crimes) or up to 3 years.
New Law (BNS 249): Up to 5 years and fine for capital offenses; up to 3 years and fine for offenses punishable with life.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Bailable | Magistrate of First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Citizens must not provide transport or hiding places to individuals wanted under non-bailable warrants or proclaimed absconders.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever harbours or conceals a person whom he knows or has reason to believe to be the offender, with the intention of screening him from legal punishment, commits an offense under Section 249.

laws.subject: Causing Disappearance of Evidence / Giving False Information
laws.description: Destroying physical, chemical, or electronic evidence of an offense, or giving information known to be false to screen an offender from legal punishment.
laws.key_changes: Explicitly encompasses digital devices, wiping server logs, deleting chats, and destroying electronic evidence.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 201): Up to 7 years (for capital offenses), 3 years, or 1/4th of maximum term.
New Law (BNS 238): Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine for capital crimes; up to 3 years for life terms.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Bailable | Court of Session / Magistrate of First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Never delete digital evidence, formatted disks, or CCTV logs after a crime has occurred; forensic retrieval will uncover intentional tampering.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever causes any evidence of an offense to disappear, or gives false information respecting the offense with intent to screen the offender, shall be punished under Section 238 BNS.

laws.subject: Theft and Snatching
laws.description: Moving movable property out of the possession of any person without consent. Section 304 creates a brand new offense of Snatching (sudden or quick seizing of property).
laws.key_changes: First time 'Snatching' is separated from simple theft into a distinct aggravated statutory offense under Section 304 BNS.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 379): Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
New Law: BNS 303 (Theft): Up to 3 years, fine, or community service. BNS 304 (Snatching): Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Theft & Snatching are Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Any Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Snatching of mobile phones, chains, or purses should be specifically reported under Section 304 BNS rather than generic lost property reports.
laws.full_statutory_text: Section 303: Whoever dishonestly takes movable property commits theft. Section 304: Theft is snatching if offender suddenly or quickly grabs or takes away property from any person.

laws.subject: Extortion
laws.description: Intentionally putting any person in fear of any injury to that person or to any other, and thereby dishonestly inducing delivery of property or valuable security.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned to Section 308 BNS. Covers digital blackmail, sextortion, cyber-extortion, and ransom threats.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 384): Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
New Law (BNS 308): Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine; extending to 10 years if death or grievous hurt threatened.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Magistrate of First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Preserve all extortion messages, bank account details where ransom was demanded, and register a complaint on cybercrime.gov.in (1930) or local police.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever intentionally puts any person in fear of any injury and thereby dishonestly induces the delivery of any property commits extortion under Section 308 BNS.

laws.subject: Robbery and Dacoity
laws.description: Theft or extortion involving the causing of death, hurt, or wrongful restraint. When committed by five or more persons conjointly, it constitutes Dacoity.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned to Sections 309 and 310 BNS with stringent minimum imprisonment terms.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law: IPC 392 (up to 10 years), IPC 395 (Life imprisonment or up to 10 years).
New Law: BNS 309 (Robbery: Up to 10-14 years); BNS 310 (Dacoity: Life imprisonment or rigorous imprisonment up to 10 years, and fine).
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Court of Session.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Emergency police hotline 112 should be alerted immediately. Test identification parades (TIP) under Section 54 BNSS are conducted to verify perpetrators.
laws.full_statutory_text: In all robbery there is either theft or extortion with violence. When five or more persons conjointly commit or attempt robbery, every member commits dacoity under Section 310 BNS.

laws.subject: Criminal Breach of Trust
laws.description: Being entrusted with property or dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriating, converting to one's own use, or disposing of that property in violation of law or legal contract.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned from IPC 406 to Section 316 BNS. Clarifies liability of directors, partners, bankers, and trustees handling public investment funds.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 406): Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both.
New Law (BNS 316(2)): Imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both; up to life or 10 years if committed by public servants or bankers.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Magistrate of First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Provide deposit receipts, trust agreements, or partnership deeds demonstrating initial entrustment and subsequent dishonest diversion of funds.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever being in any manner entrusted with property dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property commits criminal breach of trust under Section 316 BNS.

laws.subject: Cheating and Dishonestly Inducing Delivery of Property
laws.description: Deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly inducing the person to deliver any property, make, alter, or destroy any valuable security.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned from famous IPC Section 420 to BNS Section 318(4). Covers financial scams, online fraud, bogus investment schemes, and corporate deceit.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 420): Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
New Law (BNS 318(4)): Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Magistrate of First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: File complaint with proof of initial fraudulent inducement (emails, advertisements, forged documents) and banking trails showing money transfer.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property commits an offense under Section 318(4) BNS and shall be punished with imprisonment up to seven years.

laws.subject: Mischief and Property Destruction
laws.description: Doing an act with intent to cause wrongful loss or damage to the public or to any person by destroying or diminishing the value or utility of property.
laws.key_changes: Monetary thresholds for damage updated from archaic colonial amounts to modern standards; community service introduced for minor mischief.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 427): Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
New Law (BNS 324): Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or community service; extending to 5 years if public infrastructure damaged.
laws.procedural_classification: Non-Cognizable (if minor) / Cognizable (if public property) | Bailable | Any Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Photograph all damaged property, obtain repair estimates, and report to police or file civil damages claim before the competent court.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever with intent to cause wrongful loss destroys or diminishes the utility of property commits mischief under Section 324 BNS.

laws.subject: Criminal Trespass and Housebreaking (Illegal Encroachment)
laws.description: Entering into or upon property in the possession of another with intent to commit an offense, or to intimidate, insult, or annoy any person in possession.
laws.key_changes: Modernized under Sections 329-333 BNS with enhanced penalties for housebreaking at night and illegal land grabbing.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 447/448): Imprisonment up to 3 months to 1 year.
New Law (BNS 333): Imprisonment up to 1 to 2 years and fine; extending to 10 years if armed with deadly weapons.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Bailable (simple trespass) / Non-Bailable (housebreaking by night) | Any Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Property owners facing illegal encroachment should produce title deeds, mutation records, and police complaints to seek eviction under Section 164 BNSS.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever enters property in possession of another with intent to commit an offense or intimidate the possessor commits criminal trespass under Section 329 BNS.

laws.subject: Forgery and Forgery for Purpose of Cheating
laws.description: Making any false document or false electronic record with intent to cause damage or injury to the public or any person, or to support any claim or title.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned to Sections 336 and 338 BNS. Explicitly applies to forged electronic signatures, altered digital documents, and electronic records.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 468): Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
New Law (BNS 338): Imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Magistrate of First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Submit original and forged documents for forensic handwriting and digital authenticity analysis by the State Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL).
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever makes a false document or electronic record with intent to support any claim or deceive commits forgery under Section 336 BNS; if for purpose of cheating, Section 338 applies.

laws.subject: Cruelty by Husband or Relatives of Husband
laws.description: Subjecting a woman to cruelty, defined as wilful conduct driving her to suicide or causing grave injury, or harassment to coerce unlawful demands for dowry.
laws.key_changes: Split into Section 85 (punishment for cruelty) and Section 86 (detailed statutory definition of physical and mental cruelty). Arnesh Kumar notice safeguards apply under Section 35(3) BNSS.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 498A): Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.
New Law (BNS 85): Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Non-Compoundable (without court permission) | Magistrate of First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Victims can concurrently seek protection orders and residence under Domestic Violence Act Section 12. Notice of appearance under Section 35(3) BNSS applies prior to arrest.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever, being the husband or relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years and fine under Section 85 BNS.

laws.subject: Sexual Intercourse by Deceitful Means (False Promise of Marriage)
laws.description: Employing deceitful means, including false promises of employment, promotion, or marriage under suppressive identity, to have sexual intercourse.
laws.key_changes: Brand new statutory provision. Resolves decades of conflicting case law regarding consensual relationships versus deceitful promises to marry.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law: Charged under rape (IPC 376) or cheating (IPC 417).
New Law (BNS 69): Imprisonment for a term which may extend to 10 years, and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Court of Session.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Distinguishes genuine broken engagements from fraudulent inducement with intent to deceive from inception.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever by deceitful means or by making promise to marry a woman without any intention of fulfilling the same has sexual intercourse shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years and fine.

laws.subject: Rape and Aggravated Rape
laws.description: Sexual intercourse or non-consensual penetration of a woman without her consent or against her will, or under fear of death, hurt, or intoxication.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned to Sections 63 and 64 BNS. Mandatory minimum sentence is 10 years extending to life imprisonment.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 376): Rigorous imprisonment not less than 10 years, extending to life.
New Law (BNS 64): Rigorous imprisonment not less than 10 years extending to life imprisonment, and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Non-Compoundable | Exclusively Court of Session.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Victim's statement must be recorded by a woman police officer and Magistrate under Section 183 BNSS. Medical examination must be completed within 24 hours.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever commits rape shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term which shall not be less than ten years, but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and fine.

laws.subject: Gang Rape and Gang Rape of a Minor
laws.description: Rape committed by one or more persons acting in furtherance of a common intention. Section 70(2) specifically penalizes gang rape of a girl under 18 years of age.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned to Section 70 BNS. Section 70(2) mandates imprisonment for natural life or death for gang rape of a minor girl.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 376D): Min. 20 years extending to natural life.
New Law: BNS 70(1): Min. 20 years extending to life. BNS 70(2) (minor girl): Imprisonment for remainder of natural life or Death.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Court of Session.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Free legal aid from DLSA advocate is mandatory for the victim. In-camera trial and identity protection under Section 73 BNS is strictly enforced.
laws.full_statutory_text: Where a woman is raped by one or more persons constituting a group, each person is deemed to have committed gang rape under Section 70 BNS and shall face min. 20 years to life or death.

laws.subject: Assault to Outrage Modesty & Sexual Harassment
laws.description: Assaulting or using criminal force to any woman intending to outrage her modesty; physical contact involving unwelcome sexual overtures, demands for sexual favours, or showing pornography.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned to Sections 74 and 75 BNS. Explicitly applies to verbal and digital sexual harassment.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law: IPC 354 (1 to 5 years), IPC 354A (1 to 3 years).
New Law: BNS 74 (1 to 5 years and fine); BNS 75 (up to 1 to 3 years, fine, or both).
laws.procedural_classification: Section 74 is Non-Bailable; Section 75(1) is Bailable | Cognizable | Any Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Preserve all electronic messages, call recordings, and eyewitness statements. Workplaces must also have an active Internal Complaints Committee under POSH Act.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any woman intending to outrage her modesty shall be punished under Section 74 with imprisonment up to five years. Section 75 covers sexual harassment.

laws.subject: Assault with Intent to Disrobe and Voyeurism
laws.description: Assaulting a woman to compel her to be naked; watching or capturing the image of a woman engaging in a private act where she has expectation of privacy.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned to Sections 76 and 77 BNS. Covers modern surveillance, hidden cameras, spy cams, and non-consensual internet dissemination.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law: IPC 354B (3 to 7 years), IPC 354C (1 to 3 years first conviction).
New Law: BNS 76 (3 to 7 years and fine); BNS 77 (1 to 3 years first offense, up to 7 years on repeat).
laws.procedural_classification: BNS 76 is Non-Bailable; BNS 77 is Bailable on first offense | Cognizable | Any Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Report secretly installed hidden cameras in fitting rooms, hotel rooms, or shared rentals to local police for forensic hardware seizure under Section 105 BNSS.
laws.full_statutory_text: Section 76 penalizes assault to disrobe with imprisonment from 3 to 7 years. Section 77 penalizes voyeurism and non-consensual capturing or disseminating images of private acts.

laws.subject: Stalking (Physical and Cyberstalking)
laws.description: Following a woman and contacting or attempting to contact her repeatedly despite clear disinterest; monitoring a woman's use of internet, email, or digital communication.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned to Section 78 BNS with comprehensive coverage of GPS tracking, spyware, social media harassment, and electronic stalking.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 354D): Imprisonment up to 3 years (first offense) and 5 years (repeat).
New Law (BNS 78): Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine for first conviction; up to 5 years for second conviction.
laws.procedural_classification: Bailable on first conviction; Non-Bailable on second conviction | Cognizable | Any Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Take screenshots with date and time stamps of messages, social media handles, call logs, and register complaint under Section 78 BNS and Section 66D IT Act.
laws.full_statutory_text: Any man who follows a woman and contacts her repeatedly despite indication of disinterest, or monitors her internet usage, commits stalking under Section 78 BNS.

laws.subject: Defamation and Community Service Reform
laws.description: Making or publishing any imputation concerning any person intending to harm the reputation of such person by words spoken, written, signs, or visible representations.
laws.key_changes: Community service is formally introduced as an alternative punishment to imprisonment, preventing frivolous criminal defamation from burdening prisons.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 500): Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
New Law (BNS 356): Simple imprisonment up to 2 years, or with fine, or with both, or with community service.
laws.procedural_classification: Non-Cognizable | Bailable | Compoundable | Court of Session / Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Truth for public good (Exception 1) and fair criticism of public conduct are complete legal defenses against defamation charges.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever defames another shall be punished with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both, or with community service under Section 356 BNS.

laws.subject: Criminal Intimidation and Intentional Insult
laws.description: Threatening another person with injury to person, reputation, or property, or to the person or reputation of anyone in whom that person is interested, to compel an act.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned to Sections 351 and 352 BNS. Enhanced penalties for anonymous threats and digital intimidation.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 506): Up to 2 years or fine; up to 7 years if threat to cause death or grievous hurt.
New Law (BNS 351): Up to 2 years or fine; up to 7 years if threat is to cause death, grievous hurt, or destruction of property.
laws.procedural_classification: Non-Cognizable (Part I) / Cognizable (Part II - death threats) | Bailable | Any Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Record and timestamp threatening voice calls or preserve messages to substantiate Section 351 charges before the police or Magistrate.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever threatens another with injury to person, reputation, or property commits criminal intimidation under Section 351 BNS and shall be punished with up to seven years.

laws.subject: Criminal Conspiracy
laws.description: When two or more persons agree to do, or cause to be done, an illegal act or an act which is not illegal by illegal means.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned from IPC 120B to BNS Section 61(2). Agreement between conspirators constitutes the crime without requiring completion of primary offense.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law (IPC 120B): Punished in same manner as if offender abetted the offense.
New Law (BNS 61(2)): Punished in same manner as abetment of that offense.
laws.procedural_classification: Depends on the primary offense planned (Cognizable/Non-Bailable if primary offense is so).
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Circumstantial evidence, common bank accounts, meeting logs, and co-conspirator calls are evaluated to prove meeting of minds under Section 61.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever is a party to a criminal conspiracy to commit an offense punishable with death, life imprisonment or rigorous imprisonment for two years or upwards shall be punished as an abettor.

laws.subject: Joint Liability (Acts Done in Furtherance of Common Intention)
laws.description: When a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, each of such persons is liable for that act in the same manner as if it were done by him alone.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned from famous IPC Section 34 to BNS Section 3(5). Establishes principle of joint constructive liability.
laws.punishment_comparison:
Old Law: IPC 34.
New Law: BNS Section 3(5). Same punishment as the substantive offense committed.
laws.procedural_classification: Follows the substantive offense committed by the group.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Requires proof of pre-arranged plan or prior concert and active physical participation in execution of the crime.
laws.full_statutory_text: When a criminal act is done by several persons in furtherance of the common intention of all, each of such persons is liable for that act as if done by him alone under Section 3(5) BNS.

laws.subject: First Information Report (FIR) & Zero FIR
laws.description: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offense must be reduced to writing by the police officer. Zero FIR allows recording at ANY police station irrespective of territory.
laws.key_changes: Zero FIR concept formally codified into statutory law. Electronic FIR (e-FIR) introduced under Section 173(1)(ii). Police must provide free copy of FIR immediately to informant.
laws.punishment_comparison: Procedural mandate. Police officer refusing to record FIR faces prosecution under Section 199 BNS (up to 2 years imprisonment).
laws.procedural_classification: Statutory Duty of Police | Universal Jurisdiction for Zero FIR.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: If a police station refuses to file an FIR, demand a Zero FIR or send your complaint via registered post or email to Superintendent of Police (SP) under Section 173(4) BNSS.
laws.full_statutory_text: Every information relating to a cognizable offense may be given orally or electronically. Zero FIR shall be registered irrespective of jurisdiction and transferred to the competent station.

laws.subject: Information Given by Electronic Communication (e-FIR)
laws.description: Filing of criminal complaints and information regarding cognizable offenses through electronic communication, mobile apps, or state police portals.
laws.key_changes: Brand new statutory mechanism. Citizen can file e-FIR from anywhere; required to sign within three days before investigation formally begins.
laws.punishment_comparison: Procedural provision.
laws.procedural_classification: Digital Procedural Remedy | 3-day signature requirement.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: When filing an e-FIR online, remember to visit the designated police station or sign electronically within 3 days for the investigation to proceed.
laws.full_statutory_text: Information given through electronic communication shall be taken on record by police, provided that it shall be signed within three days by the person giving it.

laws.subject: Preliminary Inquiry Before FIR
laws.description: Police officer may conduct a preliminary inquiry in offenses punishable with 3 to 7 years to ascertain whether a prima facie cognizable case exists, within 14 days.
laws.key_changes: Codifies the Lalita Kumari exception into written statute. Inquiry must be concluded within 14 days with prior permission of an officer not below Deputy SP.
laws.punishment_comparison: Statutory safeguard against arbitrary or malicious prosecution.
laws.procedural_classification: Statutory Procedure | Maximum 14-day timeline with DSP approval.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Applies primarily to matrimonial disputes, commercial cases, medical negligence, and cases with abnormal delay in reporting.
laws.full_statutory_text: In offenses punishable with 3 to 7 years, the police officer may with prior permission of an officer not below rank of DSP conduct preliminary inquiry within 14 days.

laws.subject: Mandatory Forensic Investigation for Serious Crimes (7+ Years)
laws.description: In all offenses punishable with imprisonment for seven years or more, the investigating officer must cause a forensic expert to visit the crime scene to collect evidence.
laws.key_changes: Groundbreaking procedural reform. Forensic crime scene visit and videography of evidence collection are now mandatory under statutory law.
laws.punishment_comparison: Mandatory investigative standard.
laws.procedural_classification: Statutory Investigative Mandate for all 7+ year offenses.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Victims and witnesses must protect the physical crime scene from contamination until the scientific forensics team arrives.
laws.full_statutory_text: On information of offense punishable for seven years or more, forensic expert shall visit crime scene, collect scientific evidence, and videograph the process on mobile or electronic device.

laws.subject: Arrest of Persons Without Warrant & Display of Arrest Memo
laws.description: Specifies strict grounds when police may arrest without a warrant and mandates preparation of an arrest memo signed by at least one family member or witness.
laws.key_changes: Integrates D.K. Basu arrest guidelines into statute. Mandatory display of designated police officer in every district and police station.
laws.punishment_comparison: Illegal detention renders police officers liable to departmental action and prosecution.
laws.procedural_classification: Constitutional & Statutory Arrest Safeguard.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Every arrested citizen has the right to have one relative or friend informed immediately and to undergo medical checkup every 48 hours under Section 53 BNSS.
laws.full_statutory_text: A police officer arresting any person shall prepare an arrest memo attested by at least one witness, and inform the arrestee of his right to inform a friend or relative.

laws.subject: Notice of Appearance in Offenses Punishable up to 7 Years
laws.description: Police officer shall issue a Notice of Appearance to the accused where arrest is not required for offenses punishable with imprisonment up to seven years.
laws.key_changes: Reinforces Arnesh Kumar guidelines. Police must record specific written reasons if they decide to arrest an accused who complies with the appearance notice.
laws.punishment_comparison: Arrest without recording statutory reasons violates Section 35(3) BNSS.
laws.procedural_classification: Mandatory Pre-Arrest Procedure for offenses < 7 years.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: If you receive a Section 35(3) Notice of Appearance, appear before the Investigating Officer with legal counsel; compliance protects you from custodial arrest.
laws.full_statutory_text: The police officer shall issue a notice directing the person against whom reasonable complaint is made to appear before him if arrest is not required under Section 35(1).

laws.old_law: CrPC, 1973 - No dedicated age-specific arrest permission
laws.subject: Arrest Safeguards for Senior Citizens (60+) and Infirm Persons
laws.description: No arrest can be made for offenses punishable with less than three years in case of a person who is infirm or over sixty years of age, without prior permission.
laws.key_changes: Historic welfare protection. Police must obtain prior written permission from an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) before arresting senior citizens.
laws.punishment_comparison: Protective statutory bar against arbitrary arrest.
laws.procedural_classification: Mandatory Senior Citizen & Infirm Protection.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Senior citizens (aged 60+) facing minor disputes cannot be arbitrarily arrested by junior police officers without senior supervisory approval.
laws.full_statutory_text: No arrest shall be made without prior permission of an officer not below rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police in case of offense punishable for less than 3 years if person is infirm or over sixty.

laws.old_law: Judicial Precedents (Prem Shankar Shukla v. Delhi Admin)
laws.subject: Restrictions on Use of Handcuffs
laws.description: Police officer may use handcuffs only when necessary for habitual or repeat offenders, persons accused of heinous crimes like murder, rape, terrorist acts, or escaping custody.
laws.key_changes: Statutorily regulates the use of handcuffs, restricting them to grave offenses and preventing routine humiliation of undertrials in court.
laws.punishment_comparison: Unlawful handcuffing violates Article 21 and Section 43(3) BNSS.
laws.procedural_classification: Human Rights Procedural Safeguard.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Under Section 43(3), police cannot handcuff ordinary economic or non-violent accused persons unless specific flight risk or violence is proven to the Magistrate.
laws.full_statutory_text: The police officer may keep in mind the nature of offense and use handcuffs only for persons accused of heinous offenses, escape from custody, or organized crime.

laws.subject: Mandatory Audio-Video Recording of Search and Seizure
laws.description: All searches of premises, seizure of property, and preparation of seizure memos by police must be recorded through audio-video electronic means, preferably mobile phone.
laws.key_changes: Transformative transparency reform. Paper-only searches prone to planting of false evidence are replaced by mandatory digital recording submitted to the Magistrate within 48 hours.
laws.punishment_comparison: Search and seizure without videography can be challenged for procedural illegality.
laws.procedural_classification: Mandatory Evidence Integrity Standard for all police searches.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Citizens have the right to demand that police videograph any home or business search and provide a signed copy of the seizure list on the spot.
laws.full_statutory_text: The process of conducting search of a place or seizure of property shall be recorded through any audio-video electronic means and forwarded without delay to the Magistrate.

laws.subject: Police Custody Duration & Judicial Custody Limits
laws.description: Regulates the maximum duration of police custody remand (up to 15 days) and judicial custody during ongoing criminal investigation.
laws.key_changes: Police custody of up to 15 days can now be granted in whole or in parts during the initial 40 days (for 60-day cases) or 60 days (for 90-day cases).
laws.punishment_comparison: Procedural custody parameters.
laws.procedural_classification: Judicial Remand Procedure | Scrutinized by Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: An accused must be produced before the nearest Judicial Magistrate within 24 hours of arrest excluding journey time.
laws.full_statutory_text: Magistrate may authorize detention in police custody for a term not exceeding fifteen days in the whole, or in parts, during the first forty or sixty days of investigation.

laws.subject: Default Bail (Statutory Indefeasible Right to Release)
laws.description: Mandatory release of the accused on bail if the police fail to file a chargesheet within 90 days (for offenses punishable by death, life, or 10+ years) or 60 days (for other offenses).
laws.key_changes: Preserves the indefeasible right to default bail under Section 187(3) BNSS as an absolute statutory safeguard against endless police delay.
laws.punishment_comparison: Statutory right to liberty.
laws.procedural_classification: Absolute Statutory Right to Bail on expiry of 60/90 days.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: If the police do not submit the chargesheet on day 61 or 91, the accused must immediately file a default bail application before the Magistrate.
laws.full_statutory_text: The accused person shall be released on bail if he is prepared to and does furnish bail, on expiry of 90 days or 60 days where investigation has not been completed.

laws.subject: Undertrial Bail Rights for First-Time Offenders
laws.description: Release of undertrial prisoners who have spent one-third (for first-time offenders) or one-half (for other offenders) of the maximum period of imprisonment specified for the offense.
laws.key_changes: Historic undertrial relief. First-time offenders who have never been convicted before must be released on bail after serving just one-third of the maximum sentence.
laws.punishment_comparison: De-congestion of undertrial prisons.
laws.procedural_classification: Mandatory Undertrial Bail Mandate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Prison superintendents are statutorily required under Section 479(3) to apply directly to the court for release of eligible undertrial prisoners.
laws.full_statutory_text: Where a first-time offender has undergone detention for a period extending up to one-third of the maximum period of imprisonment, he shall be released by the Court on bail.

laws.subject: Regular Bail in Non-Bailable Offenses
laws.description: Discretionary power of Magistrates (Section 480) and Sessions / High Courts (Section 483) to grant bail in non-bailable criminal offenses.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned to Sections 480 and 483 BNSS. Codifies bail guidelines prioritizing personal liberty for women, sick, or infirm persons.
laws.punishment_comparison: Judicial discretion guided by statutory parameters.
laws.procedural_classification: Bail Jurisdiction | Magistrate, Sessions Court, and High Court.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Bail conditions typically require surrender of passport, cooperation with Investigating Officer, and non-tampering with prosecution witnesses.
laws.full_statutory_text: High Court or Court of Session may direct that any person accused of an offense and in custody be released on bail under Section 483 BNSS.

laws.subject: Anticipatory Bail (Direction for Grant of Bail to Person Apprehending Arrest)
laws.description: Application before the Court of Session or High Court for a direction that in the event of arrest on false, vexatious, or non-bailable charges, the applicant shall be released on bail.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned from CrPC 438 to BNSS Section 482. Incorporates the landmark 5-judge Sushila Aggarwal precedent establishing that anticipatory bail has no arbitrary time limit.
laws.punishment_comparison: Pre-arrest protective remedy.
laws.procedural_classification: Special Preventive Remedy | Court of Session and High Court.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: File anticipatory bail before the Sessions Court immediately upon learning of a false FIR or motivated police complaint before custody is effected.
laws.full_statutory_text: Where any person has reason to believe that he may be arrested on accusation of having committed a non-bailable offense, he may apply to High Court or Court of Session under Section 482.

laws.subject: Summary Trials Expansion to Offenses Up to 3 Years
laws.description: Streamlined, rapid trial of minor offenses without lengthy formal charge drafting to prevent prolonged judicial backlog.
laws.key_changes: Summary trial scope dramatically expanded from offenses punishable up to 2 years under old CrPC to offenses punishable up to 3 years under BNSS.
laws.punishment_comparison: Max sentence in summary trial is 3 months imprisonment.
laws.procedural_classification: Rapid Court Procedure | Chief Judicial Magistrate or Magistrate of First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Ensures petty offenses, minor thefts, and minor disputes are resolved within weeks rather than languishing for years.
laws.full_statutory_text: Any Magistrate of the first class may try in a summary way any offense not punishable with death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment for a term exceeding three years.

laws.old_law: CrPC, 1973 - Section 299 (Record Evidence Only; Trial Stayed)
laws.subject: Trial in Absentia of Proclaimed Absconding Offenders
laws.description: Conducting full criminal trial, examining witnesses, and pronouncing conviction and sentence in the absence of a proclaimed offender who has absconded abroad or evaded warrants.
laws.key_changes: Major statutory innovation. Fugitive economic offenders and terrorists who flee India can no longer stall their criminal trials; judgments can be delivered in absentia.
laws.punishment_comparison: Full conviction and sentence can be passed; properties confiscated.
laws.procedural_classification: Trial Procedure for Proclaimed Absconders after 90-day proclamation.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Victims of multi-crore fraud where the mastermind fled abroad can now receive court judgments and restitution orders without waiting decades for extradition.
laws.full_statutory_text: Where a person declared proclaimed offender has absconded, the Court may proceed with trial in absentia and record judgment of conviction or acquittal under Section 356 BNSS.

laws.old_law: Ad-hoc Judicial Schemes (No comprehensive CrPC chapter)
laws.subject: Witness Protection Scheme
laws.description: Every State Government is statutorily mandated to prepare and notify a Witness Protection Scheme to ensure physical protection, relocation, and anonymity for witnesses.
laws.key_changes: Statutory codification of witness rights into criminal procedure code for the first time in Indian legal history.
laws.punishment_comparison: State duty to provide protection.
laws.procedural_classification: Citizen Protection Remedy | Standing Committee in every district.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Witnesses facing threats in organized crime, rape, or murder trials can petition the District Witness Protection Committee for armed security or identity masking.
laws.full_statutory_text: Every State Government shall prepare and notify a Witness Protection Scheme for the State with a view to provide protection to witnesses under Section 398 BNSS.

laws.subject: Inherent Powers of High Court (Quashing of Frivolous FIRs)
laws.description: Inherent power of the High Court to make such orders as may be necessary to give effect to any order under this Sanhita, or to prevent abuse of the process of any court, or to secure the ends of justice.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned from famous CrPC Section 482 to BNSS Section 528. Incorporates the landmark Bhajan Lal tests for quashing false FIRs.
laws.punishment_comparison: Quashing of FIR and entire criminal proceedings.
laws.procedural_classification: Constitutional & Inherent High Court Remedy.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: If an FIR has been registered with clear malice, civil dispute turned criminal, or with zero legal evidence, file a Quashing Petition under Section 528 BNSS before the High Court.
laws.full_statutory_text: Nothing in this Sanhita shall limit or affect the inherent powers of the High Court to make such orders as may be necessary to prevent abuse of process of any court or secure ends of justice.

laws.subject: Admissibility of Electronic Records & Digital Evidence
laws.description: Information contained in an electronic record printed on paper, stored, recorded, or copied in optical or magnetic media produced by a computer shall be deemed to be a document.
laws.key_changes: Modernizes Section 65B IEA. Codifies the Arjun Khotkar 3-judge bench ruling regarding electronic certificates; simplifies digital authentication.
laws.punishment_comparison: Inadmissibility of secondary electronic evidence if certificate missing.
laws.procedural_classification: Statutory Evidence Rule | Mandatory for mobile, server, and digital logs.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Always submit an electronic certificate under Section 63 BSA signed by the person in lawful custody of the phone, server, or computer when presenting printouts or CCTV footage in court.
laws.full_statutory_text: Any information contained in an electronic record shall be deemed to be a document and admissible in evidence if conditions in Section 63 BSA are satisfied and certified.

laws.old_law: Indian Evidence Act, 1872 - Section 62 (Physical Documents Only)
laws.subject: Primary Evidence Expanded to Digital Devices & Cloud Storage
laws.description: Primary evidence means the document itself produced for inspection. Explanation 4 establishes that electronic records produced in multiple parts, devices, or cloud sync constitute primary evidence.
laws.key_changes: Groundbreaking shift. The original smartphone, hard drive, or simultaneously synchronized cloud file is now recognized directly as primary evidence.
laws.punishment_comparison: Primary evidence requires no Section 63 secondary certificate.
laws.procedural_classification: Foundational Rule of Evidence.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Producing the actual mobile phone or original laptop in court where the message was sent allows it to be marked as primary evidence directly under Section 57.
laws.full_statutory_text: Where an electronic record is created or stored in multiple files, each such file is primary evidence. Where stored in digital space, each printout or retrieval is primary evidence.

laws.subject: Confessions to Police Officers (Inadmissibility Rule)
laws.description: No confession made to a police officer shall be proved as against a person accused of any offense, nor while in police custody unless in immediate presence of a Magistrate.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned to Section 23 BSA. Strictly preserves the golden constitutional rule preventing custodial torture or coerced police confessions from being admitted as evidence.
laws.punishment_comparison: Coerced confessions cannot be used for conviction.
laws.procedural_classification: Fundamental Evidentiary Safeguard against custodial coercion.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Statements made while in police custody have zero legal evidentiary value in court unless recorded before a Judicial Magistrate under Section 183 BNSS.
laws.full_statutory_text: No confession made to a police officer shall be proved as against a person accused of any offense under Section 23(1) BSA.

laws.subject: Recovery of Material Facts from Accused Custody (Discovery Rule)
laws.description: When any fact is deposed to as discovered in consequence of information received from an accused in police custody, so much of such information as relates distinctly to the fact discovered may be proved.
laws.key_changes: Preserves the famous Section 27 IEA discovery exception with mandatory audio-video recording requirement under BNSS Section 105.
laws.punishment_comparison: Only the discovery of physical object is admissible.
laws.procedural_classification: Exception to Custodial Inadmissibility.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Recovery of murder weapons, stolen property, or hidden documents must be witnessed by independent panchas and videographed to withstand judicial scrutiny.
laws.full_statutory_text: When any fact is deposed to as discovered in consequence of information received from an accused in custody of police, so much of information relating distinctly to fact discovered may be proved.

laws.subject: Dying Declarations (Statements as to Cause of Death)
laws.description: Statements made by a person as to the cause of his death, or as to any of the circumstances of the transaction which resulted in his death, in cases where the cause of death comes into question.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned to Section 26 BSA. Retains high evidentiary sanctity; audio-video recording by Magistrate or medical officer is prioritized.
laws.punishment_comparison: Can form sole basis of conviction if found truthful and voluntary.
laws.procedural_classification: Substantive Exception to Hearsay Rule.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Dying declarations should ideally be recorded by an Executive Magistrate with medical certification of fitness of mind, but oral declarations to doctors or nurses are also admissible.
laws.full_statutory_text: Statements, written or verbal, of relevant facts made by a person who is dead are relevant when statement is made by person as to cause of his death under Section 26 BSA.

laws.subject: Expert Opinions (Forensic, Ballistic, Digital & DNA Evidence)
laws.description: When the Court has to form an opinion upon a point of foreign law, science, art, handwriting, finger impressions, or digital forensics, opinions of persons specially skilled are relevant.
laws.key_changes: Transitioned to Section 39 BSA. Explicitly incorporates digital forensics experts, cyber auditors, and DNA profiling specialists.
laws.punishment_comparison: Corroborative scientific evidence.
laws.procedural_classification: Expert Testimony Standard.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: In medical negligence or scientific fraud cases, independent expert committee opinions under Section 39 BSA are decisive in establishing liability.
laws.full_statutory_text: When Court has to form opinion upon point of science, art, handwriting, finger impressions, or electronic evidence, the opinions of skilled persons are relevant facts under Section 39 BSA.

laws.subject: Dishonour of Cheque for Insufficiency of Funds (Cheque Bounce)
laws.description: Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him for discharge of debt or liability is returned by the bank unpaid due to insufficiency of funds.
laws.key_changes: Section 142(2) territorial jurisdiction strictly fixed at the payee's home bank branch. Interim compensation up to 20% authorized under Section 143A.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or both.
laws.procedural_classification: Non-Cognizable | Bailable | Compoundable | Judicial Magistrate of First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Send a formal Statutory Demand Notice within 30 days of memo receipt giving 15 days to pay; file court complaint within 30 days thereafter.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever draws a cheque for discharge of debt which is returned unpaid for insufficiency of funds shall be deemed to have committed an offense punishable with up to 2 years or twice the amount.

laws.subject: Cyber Identity Theft and Online Impersonation
laws.description: Fraudulently or dishonestly making use of electronic signature, password, or unique identification feature of any other person, or cheating by personation using computer resource.
laws.key_changes: Cross-referenced with BNS Section 318 for digital fraud. Financial cybercrime hotline 1930 coordinates immediate freezing of defrauded bank funds.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 3 years and fine up to Rs. 1 Lakh.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Bailable | Any Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Report cyber financial fraud within the golden hour to 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in to initiate suspect account freezing across banks.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever fraudulently makes use of electronic signature, password, or cheats by personation using computer resource shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years and fine.

laws.old_law: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012
laws.subject: Child Sexual Abuse and Mandatory Reporting
laws.description: Penetrative and aggravated penetrative sexual assault on a child under 18 years. Section 19 imposes a mandatory statutory duty on any person to report sexual offenses against children.
laws.key_changes: Strict liability offenses. Mandatory minimum 20 years extending to life imprisonment or death. Failure of institutions or teachers to report attracts criminal penalty under Section 21.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment for not less than 20 years extending to remainder of natural life or Death, and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable | Special POCSO Court.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Child identity must be protected under Section 33. All statements are recorded in friendly child environments without uniform police presence.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever commits aggravated penetrative sexual assault on a child shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for not less than twenty years extending to life or death.

laws.old_law: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985
laws.new_law: NDPS Act, 1985 - Section 20, 21 & Section 37 Bail Bar
laws.subject: Possession and Commercial Trafficking of Banned Substances
laws.description: Cultivation, production, manufacture, possession, sale, purchase, transport, or storage of cannabis, heroin, cocaine, MDMA, or synthetic psychotropic drugs.
laws.key_changes: Stringent statutory reverse-burden of proof under Section 54. Section 37 imposes strict twin bail conditions for commercial quantities.
laws.punishment_comparison: Small quantity: Up to 1 year or Rs. 10,000 fine. Commercial quantity: Rigorous imprisonment 10 to 20 years and fine of Rs. 1 to 2 Lakhs.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable | Non-Bailable (for commercial quantity) | Special NDPS Court.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Strict search compliance under Section 50 NDPS requires offering the suspect the option to be searched before a Gazetted Officer or Magistrate.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever produces, possesses, sells or transports manufactured drugs shall face up to twenty years rigorous imprisonment and fine up to two lakh rupees for commercial quantities.

laws.old_law: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
laws.subject: Domestic Violence Protection, Residence Orders & Monetary Relief
laws.description: Provides civil and quasi-criminal remedies for women facing physical, sexual, verbal, emotional, or economic abuse in a shared domestic household.
laws.key_changes: Enables ex-parte emergency protection orders within 3 days. Right to reside in shared household cannot be denied by in-laws.
laws.punishment_comparison: Breach of protection order is an arrestable offense under Section 31 (imprisonment up to 1 year and Rs. 20,000 fine).
laws.procedural_classification: Quasi-Criminal | Immediate Magistrate Relief | Section 31 Breach is Cognizable & Non-Bailable.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Aggrieved women can approach the Protection Officer, service provider, or Magistrate directly for free legal representation and interim maintenance.
laws.full_statutory_text: An aggrieved person or Protection Officer may present an application to the Magistrate seeking protection orders, residence orders, or monetary relief under Section 12 PWDVA.

laws.old_law: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
laws.subject: Senior Citizen Maintenance & Property Transfer Revocation
laws.description: Obligation of adult children and legal heirs to maintain senior parents (60+). Section 23 enables declaring transfers of property made by senior citizens void if children fail to provide basic amenities.
laws.key_changes: Speedy summary inquiry before Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) Tribunal. Gift deeds or property transfers revoked if elderly parents are abandoned.
laws.punishment_comparison: Abandonment of senior citizen is punishable with imprisonment up to 3 months or fine (Section 24). Property transfers revoked under Section 23.
laws.procedural_classification: Summary Tribunal Procedure | SDM Maintenance Tribunal.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Senior citizens facing abandonment or denied maintenance can file a petition directly before the SDM Tribunal without paying advocate fees.
laws.full_statutory_text: Where a senior citizen has transferred property subject to condition of basic amenities and transferee fails to provide, transfer of property is deemed fraudulent and declared void under Section 23.

laws.subject: Consumer Disputes, Product Liability & E-Commerce Fraud
laws.description: Redressal of complaints regarding defective goods, deficient services, misleading advertisements, and product liability against manufacturers and e-commerce platforms.
laws.key_changes: Product liability introduced holding manufacturers and delivery platforms strictly liable for harm caused. E-Daakhil enables electronic filing from home.
laws.punishment_comparison: Failure to comply with District/State Commission orders punishable with imprisonment from 1 month to 3 years or fine (Section 72).
laws.procedural_classification: Consumer Dispute Redressal Commissions (District, State, National).
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Consumers can file complaints online on e-daakhil.nic.in or register grievances on the National Consumer Helpline (1915).
laws.full_statutory_text: A consumer may file complaint before the District Commission for deficiency of service, misleading advertisements, or product liability claims under Section 35 of Consumer Protection Act 2019.

laws.new_law: Legal Services Authorities Framework (NALSA / DLSA) - Section 12
laws.subject: Right to Free Legal Aid and Counsel for Citizens
laws.description: Provides free and competent legal services to women, children, members of SC/ST, victims of trafficking, disabled persons, and undertrial prisoners.
laws.key_changes: Nationwide 24x7 toll-free helpline 15100 connected to all District Legal Services Authorities (DLSA). Empanelled advocates provided at zero cost.
laws.punishment_comparison: Statutory citizen entitlement under Article 39A of the Constitution.
laws.procedural_classification: Constitutional Legal Aid Entitlement.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Every citizen eligible under Section 12 has an absolute right to an empanelled advocate for police representation, bail, trial, and appeals by dialing 15100.
laws.full_statutory_text: Every person who has to file or defend a case shall be entitled to legal services under this Act if that person is a woman, child, member of SC/ST, or industrial workman under Section 12.

laws.new_law: Information Technology Act, 2000 - Section 43 & 66 (Read with BNS Section 318)
laws.subject: Hacking, Unauthorized Access & Computer System Tampering
laws.description: Criminalizes unauthorized access, downloading, extraction of data, malware injection, or denial of access to computer networks and databases without permission of the owner.
laws.key_changes: Integrates digital forensics under BSA Section 63 for hash value validation. Covers cloud servers, mobile databases, and automated cyber intrusion tools.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to Rs. 5,00,000, or both.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Bailable. Triable by Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Report cyber intrusion immediately to cybercrime.gov.in or dial 1930. Retain server logs, router histories, and IP access timestamps without altering the system state.
laws.full_statutory_text: If any person without permission of the owner accesses, downloads, introduces contaminants, or damages computer systems, such act constitutes an offense under Section 43 read with Section 66.

laws.new_law: Information Technology Act, 2000 - Section 66C (Identity Theft & Impersonation)
laws.subject: Identity Theft, Digital Signature Hijacking & Credential Theft
laws.description: Penalizes fraudulently or dishonestly making use of the electronic signature, password, biometric key, or unique identification feature of any other person.
laws.key_changes: Directly links to OTP theft, SIM swap fraud, and fake profile creation. Can be charged concurrently with cheating under BNS Section 318(4).
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 3 years and fine which may extend to Rs. 1,00,000.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Bailable. Triable by Judicial Magistrate First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: If your WhatsApp, email, or social media credentials are hijacked to solicit funds, register a complaint on National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (1930) and notify your contacts immediately.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever, fraudulently or dishonestly, makes use of the electronic signature, password or any other unique identification feature of any other person, shall be punished under Section 66C.

laws.new_law: Information Technology Act, 2000 - Section 66D (Cheating by Personation using Computer)
laws.subject: Cheating by Personation Using Computer Resource / Online Banking Fraud
laws.description: Punishes any person who by means of any communication device or computer resource cheats by personating another person, brand, or financial institution.
laws.key_changes: Primary penal section for UPI phishing scams, fake customer care numbers, loan app deception, and lottery/job phishing scams across India.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment of either description for a term up to 3 years and fine up to Rs. 1,00,000.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Bailable. Triable by Judicial Magistrate First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: If you are defrauded via fraudulent payment links or phone calls, report to 1930 within the 'Golden Hour' (first 2 hours) so the nodal bank cyber cell can freeze the destination account.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever, by means of any communication device or computer resource cheats by personating, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years.

laws.new_law: Information Technology Act, 2000 - Section 66E (Violation of Bodily Privacy)
laws.subject: Violation of Bodily Privacy & Non-Consensual Recording
laws.description: Penalizes capturing, publishing, or transmitting images of private areas of any person without consent under circumstances violating that person's reasonable expectation of privacy.
laws.key_changes: Strengthened evidentiary compliance for electronic messaging applications (WhatsApp, Telegram) and hidden camera / voyeurism surveillance.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to Rs. 2,00,000, or both.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Bailable. Triable by any Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Victims of hidden cameras or non-consensual image distribution can request immediate content takedown under Rule 3(2)(b) of the IT Rules, 2021 within 24 hours.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever, intentionally or knowingly captures, publishes or transmits the image of a private area of any person without his or her consent commits an offense under Section 66E.

laws.new_law: Information Technology Act, 2000 - Section 67 (Publishing Obscene Content)
laws.subject: Publishing or Transmitting Obscene Material in Electronic Form
laws.description: Criminalizes publishing, transmitting, or causing to be published in electronic form any material which is lascivious or appeals to prurient interests.
laws.key_changes: Differentiates between general adult obscenity and aggravated sexually explicit or non-consensual deepfake content.
laws.punishment_comparison: First conviction: Imprisonment up to 3 years and fine up to Rs. 5,00,000. Subsequent conviction: Imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to Rs. 10,00,000.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Bailable on first offense; Non-bailable on subsequent conviction.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Circulating defamatory or sexually vulgar content on group messaging platforms makes both the originator and active distributors liable for prosecution.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever publishes or transmits or causes to be published or transmitted in electronic form, any material which is lascivious or appeals to prurient interest shall be punished under Section 67.

laws.new_law: Information Technology Act, 2000 - Section 67A & 67B (Sexually Explicit & CSAM Offenses)
laws.subject: Sexually Explicit Material & Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM)
laws.description: Imposes severe criminal penalties for publishing, transmitting, generating, or distributing sexually explicit acts, and zero tolerance for Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM).
laws.key_changes: Section 67B operates in strict alignment with POCSO Act Section 15. Merely possessing or sharing CSAM is a severe non-bailable offense.
laws.punishment_comparison: Section 67A: Up to 5 years imprisonment and Rs. 10,00,000 fine. Section 67B: Up to 5 years (first offense) and 7 years (subsequent) with fine up to Rs. 10,00,000.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Non-Bailable. Triable by Sessions Court / Special Court.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Any encounter with CSAM or sexually explicit non-consensual material must be reported immediately on cybercrime.gov.in. Do not forward or store such files under any circumstance.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever publishes or transmits sexually explicit material, or depicts children in sexually explicit acts in electronic form, commits an aggravated offense under Section 67A and 67B.

laws.new_law: Information Technology Act, 2000 - Section 69A (Government Website / App Blocking Powers)
laws.subject: Power to Issue Directions for Blocking Public Access to Information
laws.description: Authorizes the Central Government to order intermediaries to block public access to electronic information in the interests of national sovereignty, security of the State, or public order.
laws.key_changes: Governed by the Supreme Court Shreya Singhal procedural safeguard requirements including reasoned written orders and pre-decisional hearing.
laws.punishment_comparison: Intermediary failing to comply punishable with imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Administrative statutory power with penal consequences for non-compliant intermediaries.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: App and content developers must maintain appointed Grievance Officers and comply with statutory compliance inquiries within statutory deadlines.
