laws.full_statutory_text: The Central Government may, if satisfied that it is necessary in the interest of sovereignty and integrity of India, direct any agency to block access for the public to information under Section 69A.

laws.old_law: Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 - Section 3
laws.new_law: Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 - Section 3 & 4 (Offence of Money Laundering)
laws.subject: Money Laundering, Proceeds of Crime & Asset Confiscation
laws.description: Criminalizes directly or indirectly attempting to indulge or knowingly assisting or being a party in any process or activity connected with proceeds of crime and projecting it as untainted property.
laws.key_changes: The definition of proceeds of crime includes property derived directly or indirectly from any scheduled offense listed in the PMLA Schedule.
laws.punishment_comparison: Rigorous imprisonment from 3 years to 7 years (extendable to 10 years if scheduled offense falls under NDPS Act) and mandatory fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Non-Bailable. Triable by Designated Special Court (PMLA).
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Citizens must never allow their bank accounts or PAN cards to be used as mule accounts for unknown funds or crypto conversions, as account holders are prosecuted as accomplices.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whosoever directly or indirectly attempts to indulge or knowingly assists or knowingly is a party in any process connected with proceeds of crime commits money laundering under Section 3.

laws.old_law: Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 - Section 45
laws.new_law: Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 - Section 45 (Twin Conditions for Bail)
laws.subject: Rigorous Bail Thresholds in Economic & Financial Laundering
laws.description: Mandates twin statutory conditions for grant of bail: the Public Prosecutor must be given an opportunity to oppose, and the court must be satisfied that the accused is not guilty and unlikely to commit an offense while on bail.
laws.key_changes: Upheld by the Supreme Court in Vijay Madanlal Choudhary (2022) with relaxation granted to women, sick, infirm, or accused involved in sums under Rs. 1 crore.
laws.punishment_comparison: Statutory threshold condition restricting standard judicial discretion under CrPC 439 / BNSS 483.
laws.procedural_classification: Special Statutory Limitation on Bail Jurisprudence.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Persons summoned under Section 50 PMLA by Enforcement Directorate are legally bound to state the truth and produce authorized financial records.
laws.full_statutory_text: No person accused of an offence under this Act shall be released on bail unless the Public Prosecutor has been given an opportunity to oppose and the Court is satisfied of reasonable grounds of innocence.

laws.old_law: Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978
laws.new_law: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019 (BUDS Act) - Section 3 & 21
laws.subject: Illegal Deposit Schemes, Multi-Level Marketing (MLM) & Ponzi Fraud
laws.description: Bans all unregulated deposit schemes and fraudulent multi-level marketing chains that promise unreasonable financial returns on public deposits.
laws.key_changes: Provides immediate statutory power to Competent Authorities for provisional attachment of fraudster bank accounts and properties to refund depositors.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment from 2 years up to 7 years with fine of Rs. 3,00,000 to Rs. 10,00,000; fraudulent default punishable up to 10 years and Rs. 50,00,000 fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Non-Bailable. Designated Special Court jurisdiction.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Never deposit savings with unregulated entities lacking RBI, SEBI, or state government registrations. Check the SEBI SCORES or RBI Sachet portal before investing.
laws.full_statutory_text: No deposit taker shall promote, operate, issue advertisements or accept deposits in any unregulated deposit scheme under Section 3 of the BUDS Act 2019.

laws.new_law: Prohibition of Benami Property Transactions Act, 1988 (Amended 2016) - Section 3 & 53
laws.subject: Benami Property Holding, Fictitious Titles & Confiscation
laws.description: Prohibits entering into or holding benami transactions where property is transferred to or held by a person while consideration is provided by another person for immediate or future benefit.
laws.key_changes: Empowers Initiating Officers to attach benami assets provisionally and enacts complete confiscation by the Central Government without compensation.
laws.punishment_comparison: Rigorous imprisonment from 1 year up to 7 years and fine up to 25% of the fair market value of the benami property.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Non-Bailable. Adjudicated before Special Courts.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Never purchase immovable land or register commercial property under domestic workers, employees, or third-party identities, as such properties are liable to statutory confiscation.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever enters into any benami transaction shall be guilty of the offence of benami transaction and punished with rigorous imprisonment under Section 53.

laws.old_law: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 - Section 45-IA
laws.new_law: Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934 - Section 45-IA & 58B (Unregistered NBFCs & Digital Loan Apps)
laws.subject: Unregistered Digital Lending Apps, Extortionate Loans & NBFC Compliance
laws.description: Prohibits any non-banking financial institution from commencing or carrying on business of a financial institution without obtaining a certificate of registration from the RBI.
laws.key_changes: Applied aggressively against predatory Chinese and rogue instant loan apps operating without RBI license, harassing citizens with contact list exfiltration.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment from 1 year up to 5 years and fine from Rs. 1,00,000 to Rs. 25,00,000.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable offense. Investigated by State Police Cyber Crime Cells and Economic Offences Wings (EOW).
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Never install loan apps demanding access to your full contacts, photos, or device storage. Verify that the lender is registered on the RBI list of authorized digital lending partners.
laws.full_statutory_text: No non-banking financial company shall commence or carry on the business of a non-banking financial institution without obtaining a certificate of registration issued by RBI under Section 45-IA.

laws.new_law: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 - Section 138 (Dishonour of Cheque)
laws.subject: Cheque Bounce, Insufficiency of Funds & Stop Payment Defaults
laws.description: Imposes criminal liability when a bank cheque issued for the discharge of any debt or other legally enforceable liability is returned unpaid due to insufficiency of funds.
laws.key_changes: Read with 2018 amendment: Section 143A empowers trial courts to order interim compensation up to 20% of the cheque amount during trial.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or both.
laws.procedural_classification: Non-Cognizable and Bailable. Triable by Judicial Magistrate First Class upon private complaint.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Mandatory procedure: Issue a formal statutory demand notice in writing within 30 days of the cheque return memo, giving 15 days to pay before filing a complaint within the next 30 days.
laws.full_statutory_text: Where any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money is returned by the bank unpaid, such person shall be deemed to have committed an offence under Section 138.

laws.new_law: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 - Section 141 & 148 (Corporate Cheque Liability & Appellate Deposit)
laws.subject: Cheque Bounce by Companies & Appellate Court Deposit Mandates
laws.description: Governs vicarious criminal liability of company directors, managing partners, and signatories who were in charge of and responsible for the conduct of the business at the time of cheque dishonour.
laws.key_changes: Under Section 148, the Appellate Court may order the appellant drawer to deposit a minimum of 20% of the fine or compensation awarded by the trial court.
laws.punishment_comparison: Same punishment as Section 138 applied to responsible directors and signatories.
laws.procedural_classification: Statutory corporate liability in commercial criminal proceedings.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Independent directors not involved in day-to-day financial operations must present board resolutions to seek discharge under the doctrine of personal innocence.
laws.full_statutory_text: If the person committing an offence under section 138 is a company, every person who at the time was in charge of the company shall be deemed guilty under Section 141.

laws.old_law: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 - Section 3
laws.new_law: POCSO Act, 2012 - Section 3 & 4 (Penetrative Sexual Assault on Minor)
laws.subject: Penetrative Sexual Assault on Children Under 18 Years
laws.description: Criminalizes penetrative sexual assault committed against any person below the age of eighteen years, establishing gender-neutral protection for child victims.
laws.key_changes: Strict presumption of guilt under Section 29 POCSO. Mandatory trial completion within 1 year before Designated POCSO Special Courts.
laws.punishment_comparison: Rigorous imprisonment for not less than 10 years, extendable to life imprisonment, and mandatory fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Non-Bailable. Triable exclusively by Special POCSO Court.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Victim's statement is recorded by a woman police officer at the child's residence and before a Judicial Magistrate under Section 164 CrPC / 183 BNSS without delay.
laws.full_statutory_text: A person is said to commit penetrative sexual assault if he penetrates any part of the body of a child under Section 3, punishable under Section 4.

laws.old_law: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 - Section 5
laws.new_law: POCSO Act, 2012 - Section 5 & 6 (Aggravated Penetrative Sexual Assault)
laws.subject: Aggravated Penetrative Sexual Assault on Children
laws.description: Covers child sexual assault committed by persons in positions of trust or authority (police officers, medical staff, teachers, relatives) or against children under 12 or 16 years of age.
laws.key_changes: 2019 Amendment introduced capital punishment (death penalty) as an option for aggravated penetrative sexual assault on children below twelve years.
laws.punishment_comparison: Rigorous imprisonment for not less than 20 years, extendable to imprisonment for life (meaning natural life), or death, and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Heinous offense. Cognizable, Non-Bailable, Non-Compoundable.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Emergency child helpline 1098 provides instant protective custody, emergency medical treatment, and psychological counseling in coordination with Child Welfare Committees (CWC).
laws.full_statutory_text: Aggravated penetrative sexual assault under Section 5 is punishable with rigorous imprisonment for life or death under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.

laws.old_law: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 - Section 7
laws.new_law: POCSO Act, 2012 - Section 7 & 8 (Sexual Assault on Children)
laws.subject: Non-Penetrative Sexual Assault & Physical Abuse of Children
laws.description: Penalizes touching the private parts of a child or making the child touch the sexual parts of another person with sexual intent without penetration.
laws.key_changes: Supreme Court Skin-to-Skin ruling overturned the Bombay HC judgment, affirming that physical contact with sexual intent constitutes sexual assault regardless of direct skin contact.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment of either description for not less than 3 years, extendable up to 5 years, and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Non-Bailable. Special Court jurisdiction.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Parents and school administrators must report any disclosure of inappropriate touching by a child immediately to the police or CWC without attempting internal mediation.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever, with sexual intent, touches the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child commits the offence of sexual assault under Section 7, punishable under Section 8.

laws.old_law: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 - Section 11
laws.new_law: POCSO Act, 2012 - Section 11 & 12 (Sexual Harassment of Children)
laws.subject: Sexual Harassment, Stalking & Obscene Gestures Towards Minors
laws.description: Criminalizes uttering words, making gestures, repeatedly following, or showing pornographic material to a child with sexual intent.
laws.key_changes: Extensively covers online grooming, cyber harassment, and soliciting minors through social networks or gaming platforms.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to 3 years and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Non-Bailable. Triable by Special Court.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Take screenshots and archive digital communication logs before blocking online stalkers to provide verified electronic evidence under Section 63 BSA.
laws.full_statutory_text: A person is said to commit sexual harassment upon a child under Section 11 if he utters any word or makes gestures with sexual intent, punishable under Section 12.

laws.old_law: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 - Section 19
laws.new_law: POCSO Act, 2012 - Section 19 & 21 (Mandatory Reporting of Child Offenses)
laws.subject: Mandatory Reporting Duty & Criminal Liability for Concealment
laws.description: Imposes a strict statutory obligation on any person (including teachers, doctors, hospital staff, family members) having knowledge of a sexual offense against a child to report it to police or Special Juvenile Police Unit.
laws.key_changes: Failure to report is an independent criminal offense punishable with imprisonment, preventing institutional cover-ups in boarding schools and hospitals.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment up to 6 months or fine, or both; in-charge of institutions failing to report punishable up to 1 year and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Bailable. Triable by Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Doctors and medical officers treating injured minors must immediately record a medico-legal case (MLC) and notify police; failure to do so attracts personal criminal liability.
laws.full_statutory_text: Any person who has knowledge that an offence under this Act has been committed shall provide such information to the Special Juvenile Police Unit under Section 19.

laws.old_law: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 - Section 20
laws.new_law: NDPS Act, 1985 - Section 20 (Cannabis / Ganja / Charas Offenses)
laws.subject: Possession, Cultivation, Sale & Trafficking of Cannabis (Ganja & Charas)
laws.description: Prohibits cultivating, producing, manufacturing, possessing, selling, purchasing, transporting, importing, or exporting cannabis in contravention of the Act.
laws.key_changes: Penalties are strictly graded based on quantity: Small Quantity (up to 1 kg ganja / 100g charas), Intermediate Quantity, and Commercial Quantity (20 kg ganja / 1 kg charas).
laws.punishment_comparison: Small: Rigorous imprisonment up to 1 year or Rs. 10,000 fine. Commercial: Rigorous imprisonment from 10 to 20 years and fine of Rs. 1,00,000 to Rs. 2,00,000.
laws.procedural_classification: Small: Bailable. Commercial: Cognizable, Non-Bailable, with Section 37 bail restrictions.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Commercial quantity invokes Section 37 NDPS, where bail is virtually impossible unless the court finds reasonable grounds of innocence.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever, in contravention of any provision of this Act, cultivates, produces, possesses or sells cannabis shall be punished under Section 20.

laws.old_law: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 - Section 21 & 22
laws.new_law: NDPS Act, 1985 - Section 21 & 22 (Manufactured Drugs & Psychotropic Substances)
laws.subject: Possession & Trafficking of Manufactured Drugs (Heroin, Smack, MDMA, LSD)
laws.description: Criminalizes unauthorized dealing in manufactured narcotic drugs (such as morphine, heroin, cocaine) and psychotropic substances (such as MDMA, amphetamines, alprazolam).
laws.key_changes: Strict regulatory burden of proof. Seizure protocol mandates video recording and immediate inventory certification before a Judicial Magistrate under Section 52A.
laws.punishment_comparison: Small: Rigorous imprisonment up to 1 year. Commercial: Rigorous imprisonment 10 to 20 years and fine up to Rs. 2,00,000.
laws.procedural_classification: Non-Bailable in commercial and intermediate quantities. Triable by Special NDPS Court.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Section 52A requires inventory verification before a Magistrate; lack of a Magistrate certification certificate is a strong ground for defense during trial.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever possesses, sells, purchases, or transports manufactured drugs in contravention of the Act commits an offence under Section 21 and Section 22.

laws.old_law: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 - Section 27
laws.new_law: NDPS Act, 1985 - Section 27 & 64A (Consumption of Narcotics & De-Addiction Immunity)
laws.subject: Consumption of Drugs, Addict Rehabilitation & Statutory Immunity
laws.description: Penalizes consuming any narcotic drug or psychotropic substance. However, Section 64A grants statutory immunity from prosecution to addicts who voluntarily undergo medical de-addiction.
laws.key_changes: Emphasizes public health and reformative justice by diverting addicts to government rehabilitation centers rather than penal incarceration.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to Rs. 20,000 for cocaine/heroin; up to 6 months or Rs. 10,000 for other drugs.
laws.procedural_classification: Bailable offense. Immunity granted upon certified completion of de-addiction program.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: First-time drug users can file an application under Section 64A seeking judicial diversion to a certified de-addiction facility to avoid a criminal record.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever consumes any narcotic drug or psychotropic substance shall be punishable under Section 27, subject to immunity under Section 64A for undergoing de-addiction.

laws.old_law: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 - Section 27A
laws.new_law: NDPS Act, 1985 - Section 27A (Financing Illicit Drug Traffic & Harbouring Offenders)
laws.subject: Financing Illicit Drug Trafficking & Harbouring Cartel Members
laws.description: Imposes severe punishment on any person who directly or indirectly finances any illicit narcotics activities or harbours any person engaged in illicit traffic.
laws.key_changes: Applied to financial facilitators, Hawala operators, crypto wallet providers, and premise owners renting properties to drug trafficking rings.
laws.punishment_comparison: Rigorous imprisonment for not less than 10 years, extendable to 20 years, and fine of Rs. 1,00,000 to Rs. 2,00,000.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable, Non-Bailable, subject to Section 37 bail restrictions.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Landlords and bank account holders must execute proper tenant police verification to prevent properties or accounts from being implicated in drug financing syndicates.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever indulges in financing, directly or indirectly, any illicit drug activities or harbours any person engaged in such activities shall be punishable under Section 27A.

laws.old_law: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 - Section 50
laws.new_law: NDPS Act, 1985 - Section 50 (Mandatory Procedural Safeguard for Personal Search)
laws.subject: Right of Citizen to be Searched Before Gazetted Officer or Magistrate
laws.description: Mandates that when an authorized officer is about to search any person, he must inform the person of their statutory right to be taken before the nearest Gazetted Officer or Magistrate.
laws.key_changes: Constitutional Bench in Baldev Singh held this requirement mandatory; failure to inform the suspect of this right vitiates the recovery and trial.
laws.punishment_comparison: Procedural compliance mandate on law enforcement officers.
laws.procedural_classification: Mandatory Statutory Safeguard against Evidence Planting.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: If stopped for personal narcotics search, insist on exercising your Section 50 right to be searched only in the presence of a Magistrate or Gazetted Officer.
laws.full_statutory_text: When any officer is about to search any person under the Act, he shall, if such person so requires, take him without unnecessary delay to the nearest Gazetted Officer or Magistrate under Section 50.

laws.new_law: Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (Amended 2018) - Section 7 & 7A (Public Servant Bribe Demands)
laws.subject: Demand and Acceptance of Bribe / Undue Advantage by Public Servant
laws.description: Punishes any public servant who obtains, accepts, or attempts to obtain from any person an undue advantage with the intention to perform or cause improper performance of a public duty.
laws.key_changes: 2018 amendment introduced Section 7A penalizing middlemen/touts and Section 8 making bribe givers liable unless reported within 7 days.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment for not less than 3 years, extendable to 7 years, and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Non-Bailable. Investigated by Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) and CBI.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: If a government official demands a bribe, report immediately to the State Anti-Corruption Bureau or Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) within 7 days to organize a legal trap.
laws.full_statutory_text: Any public servant who obtains or accepts or attempts to obtain from any person an undue advantage with intention to perform improperly a public duty shall be punishable under Section 7.

laws.new_law: Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (Amended 2018) - Section 13 (Criminal Misconduct by Public Servant)
laws.subject: Criminal Misconduct, Disproportionate Assets & Misappropriation
laws.description: Penalizes a public servant who dishonestly or fraudulently misappropriates public property or intentionally enriches himself illicitly during the period of his office.
laws.key_changes: Possession of assets disproportionate to known sources of lawful income constitutes direct statutory presumption of criminal misconduct.
laws.punishment_comparison: Imprisonment for not less than 4 years, extendable to 10 years, and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Non-Bailable. Designated Special Judge jurisdiction.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Citizens can lodge verified complaints detailing illicit properties of corrupt public officials with the Lokpal of India or State Lokayukta with supporting property documentation.
laws.full_statutory_text: A public servant commits criminal misconduct if he dishonestly misappropriates property entrusted to him or intentionally enriches himself illicitly under Section 13.

laws.subject: Rash and Negligent Driving on a Public Road
laws.description: Punishes driving any vehicle or riding on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life or cause hurt or injury to any person.
laws.key_changes: Modernized to cover electric vehicles, high-speed sports vehicles, and commercial transport with mandatory electronic traffic camera evidence.
laws.punishment_comparison: IPC 279: Up to 6 months imprisonment or Rs. 1,000 fine. BNS 281: Up to 6 months imprisonment or fine up to Rs. 1,000, or both.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable, Bailable. Any Magistrate.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Dashcam recordings and public CCTV footage serve as conclusive proof under Section 63 BSA to disprove false allegations of rash driving.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished under Section 281 of BNS.

laws.subject: Causing Death by Negligence (Road Accidents & Medical Negligence)
laws.description: Criminalizes causing the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide.
laws.key_changes: BNS increases standard imprisonment from 2 years (under IPC 304A) to 5 years under Section 106(1), with special statutory consideration for registered medical practitioners.
laws.punishment_comparison: IPC 304A: Imprisonment up to 2 years or fine. BNS 106(1): Imprisonment up to 5 years and fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable and Bailable. Triable by Judicial Magistrate First Class.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: In accidental death, secure mechanical inspection reports of the vehicle immediately to determine if mechanical failure occurred.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine under Section 106(1).

laws.old_law: New Offense (Not in Indian Penal Code)
laws.new_law: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 - Section 106(2) (Aggravated Hit-and-Run Offense)
laws.subject: Hit-and-Run Accidents: Fleeing Scene Without Reporting
laws.description: Imposes severe aggravated criminal punishment when an offender causes death by rash and negligent driving and escapes the scene without reporting the accident to a police officer or Magistrate.
laws.key_changes: Historic addition in BNS to curb hit-and-run fatalities. Fleeing without reporting escalates the maximum punishment to 10 years imprisonment.
laws.punishment_comparison: BNS 106(2): Imprisonment for a term which may extend to 10 years, and shall also be liable to fine.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable, Non-Bailable. Triable by Court of Session.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Drivers involved in accidents must not flee. If there is a threat of mob lynching, proceed directly to the nearest police station to report the occurrence immediately to avoid Section 106(2).
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever causes death of any person by rash and negligent driving not amounting to culpable homicide, and escapes without reporting it to a police officer or a Magistrate soon after the incident, shall be punished with imprisonment up to ten years under Section 106(2).

laws.subject: Causing Hurt / Grievous Hurt by Endangering Life or Personal Safety
laws.description: Punishes causing simple hurt or grievous hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life or personal safety.
laws.key_changes: Unified under BNS Section 125 with updated fine structures and integration with vehicular and construction site safety audits.
laws.punishment_comparison: Hurt: Imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 2,500. Grievous Hurt: Imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to Rs. 10,000.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable, Bailable, Compoundable by victim with court permission.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Victims injured in road accidents should obtain a medico-legal injury report (MLC) from a hospital stating exact wound dimensions for prosecution under Section 125.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever causes hurt or grievous hurt to any person by doing any act rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, commits an offence under Section 125 of BNS.

laws.subject: Dangerous Driving, Red-Light Jumping & Mobile Phone Usage While Driving
laws.description: Penalizes driving a motor vehicle at a speed or in a manner dangerous to the public, including jumping red lights, violating stop signs, using handheld devices, and illegal overtaking.
laws.key_changes: 2019 amendment multiplied fines fivefold and classified handheld mobile phone usage while driving as dangerous driving.
laws.punishment_comparison: First offence: Imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to Rs. 5,000. Second offence: Imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to Rs. 10,000.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable traffic offense. Compoundable on spot or before Virtual Traffic Courts.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Traffic e-challans issued via automated ANPR cameras can be contested or paid directly on vcourts.gov.in (Virtual Courts) without physical court appearance.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever drives a motor vehicle at a speed or in a manner which is dangerous to the public shall be punishable under Section 184 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

laws.new_law: Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 - Section 185 (Drunken Driving / Under Drug Influence)
laws.subject: Driving by a Drunken Person or by a Person Under the Influence of Drugs
laws.description: Prohibits driving or attempting to drive a motor vehicle if alcohol in the driver's blood exceeds 30 mg per 100 ml of blood detected in a breath analyzer test.
laws.key_changes: Zero tolerance enforcement with immediate vehicle impoundment and suspension of driving license for up to 6 months.
laws.punishment_comparison: First offence: Imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Rs. 10,000, or both. Second offence: Imprisonment up to 2 years or fine of Rs. 15,000, or both.
laws.procedural_classification: Cognizable. Police officer can arrest without warrant if breath analyzer registers positive reading.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Never drive after consuming alcohol. A breath analyzer reading above 30 mg/100 ml results in court summons; repeated violations lead to driving license cancellation.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever, while driving, has in his blood, alcohol exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml of blood detected by a breath analyser, shall be punishable under Section 185.

laws.new_law: Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 - Section 192A (Vehicle Use Without Valid Permit)
laws.subject: Using Motor Vehicle Without Valid Commercial Transport Permit
laws.description: Penalizes using a motor vehicle as a transport vehicle or commercial taxi without a valid permit issued by the Regional Transport Authority (RTO).
laws.key_changes: Strictly applies to unauthorized aggregator cabs, overload goods trucks, and private vehicles used for illegal passenger carriage.
laws.punishment_comparison: First offence: Imprisonment up to 6 months and fine up to Rs. 10,000. Subsequent offence: Imprisonment up to 1 year and fine up to Rs. 10,000.
laws.procedural_classification: Non-Bailable and Compoundable under state notifications.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Commercial vehicle owners must renew fitness certificates, National Permits, and third-party insurance online via the Parivahan Sewa portal to prevent seizure.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever drives a motor vehicle or causes or allows a motor vehicle to be used in contravention of Section 66 shall be punishable under Section 192A.

laws.new_law: Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 - Section 129 & 194D (Helmet Mandate & Child Safety)
laws.subject: Wearing of Protective Headgear & Helmet Regulations
laws.description: Mandates that every person driving or riding a motorcycle of any class shall wear protective headgear conforming to Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS).
laws.key_changes: Includes safety harness and helmet rules for children over 9 months riding as pillion passengers, along with 3-month driving license disqualification.
laws.punishment_comparison: Fine of Rs. 1,000 and disqualification for holding driving license for a period of 3 months.
laws.procedural_classification: Compoundable traffic offense.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Wear a BIS-certified ISI-marked helmet with chin strap securely fastened; unfastened chin straps are treated as riding without a helmet.
laws.full_statutory_text: Whoever drives a motorcycle or rides without wearing protective headgear shall be punishable with a fine of one thousand rupees under Section 194D.

laws.new_law: Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 - Section 166 & 168 (MACT Compensation Claims)
laws.subject: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) Compensation for Death or Injury
laws.description: Empowers victims of road accidents or their legal heirs to file an application for compensation before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal against the driver, owner, and insurer.
laws.key_changes: Mandates police to file an Detailed Accident Report (DAR) within 90 days directly with MACT to expedite compensation without citizen procedural delay.
laws.punishment_comparison: Civil compensation adjudication based on age, income, dependents, and future prospects.
laws.procedural_classification: MACT Tribunal Civil Proceeding. No court fees based on percentage of claim in most states.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Claimants can file at the tribunal having jurisdiction over the accident site or where the claimant resides. Ensure insurance policy details of offending vehicle are retrieved from FIR.
laws.full_statutory_text: An application for compensation arising out of an accident of the nature specified in section 165 may be made by the person who has sustained the injury under Section 166.

laws.new_law: Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 - Section 161 (Compensation for Hit-and-Run Victims)
laws.subject: Solatium Compensation for Victims in Hit-and-Run Motor Accidents
laws.description: Provides immediate government statutory compensation to victims or legal heirs in accidents where the identity of the offending vehicle cannot be ascertained after reasonable efforts.
laws.key_changes: Compensation dramatically increased from Rs. 25,000 to Rs. 2,00,000 in case of death, and from Rs. 12,500 to Rs. 50,000 in case of grievous hurt.
laws.punishment_comparison: Statutory relief fund administered through General Insurance Council and District Collectors.
laws.procedural_classification: Welfare Compensation Scheme without need to identify the offender.
laws.practical_citizen_advice: Submit Form I to the Sub-Divisional Magistrate / Claims Enquiry Officer within 6 months of a hit-and-run accident along with the police accident certificate for immediate solatium release.
laws.full_statutory_text: The Central Government provides compensation in respect of death of any person resulting from a hit-and-run motor accident a fixed sum of two lakh rupees under Section 161.
